title: Aggregates of ±inf and NaN: IEEE results, no raise
description: `sum` and `avg` of inf and -inf are NaN; `variance` and `stddev` of a set with an infinity are NaN; `sum(1e308, 1e308)` and `avg` are +inf, while `variance(1e308, 1e308)` is 0.0. A NaN input makes `sum`, `avg`, `variance` NaN; `min` skips it (it sorts last) and `max` returns it. None of this raises under ANSI.
`COVAR_*` and `CORR` follow `variance`: a NaN or ±inf input makes them NaN, under ANSI too.

`var_samp`, `var_pop`, `stddev_*`, `covar_*` and `corr` of values holding `+inf` or `-inf` in `x` are NaN, with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false: the NaN is `nan_creation`'s (the reference raises, D37). An infinity only in `y` leaves `var_samp(x)` finite and makes `covar_*` and `corr` NaN; a single `inf` alone gives a null sample moment and `corr`. Grouped, only the group holding the infinity is NaN.
`quantile_cont` and `median` over values holding both `-inf` and `+inf` give NaN at a fraction between the two infinite neighbours: the NaN is `nan_creation`'s (the reference raises, D37).

A variance, deviation or covariance of finite doubles whose correctly rounded value overflows is `+inf` (`var_pop`, `var_samp`, `stddev_pop`, `covar_pop`, `covar_samp` of [1e200, -1e200], ungrouped and grouped), where the reference raises (`AggFn.infAgg`, #1601). `corr` of the same values is NaN, `inf / inf`: its exact value, 1, is finite, so `float_overflow` does not apply to it, and outside `Stat.fits` (values above 2³⁹⁸) `StatProps` allows any double.
reference: `nan_creation`: raise (#257); a statistical aggregate of ±inf raises (`nan_creation`); a sum past the largest double raises (#575). ST-3 and ST-5 record that Substrait leaves both open. Spark needs guards.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `sum` of NaN is NaN, no error under ANSI
